note: Lanes of the stability lab (plans/cmux-next/chrome-parity/p10-stability.md, section 3.A). stability-lab.py reads id and tier; the runner (task 003) reads the rest. Every lane runs through cmux-ci at the lowest priority, never on a bench host, and blocks no push, merge or nightly.

lanes.summary: cargo-fuzz, 5 minutes per cmux-tui/fuzz target, each from its stored corpus; the run's corpus is minimized (-merge=1) and stored back.

corpus.carry: {corpus_in} is the newest passed rust-fuzz or rust-fuzz-coverage step's artifact, uploaded for this step's lane with `cmux-ci artifact-put` (store objects live 14 days; the daily run refreshes it). The step's --store is a fresh directory in its checkout, so the corpus moves with the lane, not with the host. With no earlier artifact the lane drops --store-import and starts from the seeds.

lanes.findings: summary.jsonl verdicts crash, oom, timeout and leak; each artifact goes through crash_signature.py and stability_issues.py. The fix commits `rust-fuzz.sh --minimize-crash TARGET FILE`, a regression input of at most 64 KiB under cmux-tui/fuzz/corpus/<target>/.

lanes.summary: cargo fuzz coverage + llvm-cov of every target's stored corpus; covered regions go into the store's history, and a target flat over its last 3 measurements gets one fuzz-quality issue.

corpus.carry: the same {corpus_in} as rust-fuzz; its exported store carries the coverage history to the next run.
